chapter_title: Concerning the Light Mind and the Apostles and the Saints
chapter_note: This long chapter has a clearly substratic first two-thirds (¶11-42) containing the quintessential body-cosmos correspondence and the five-fold soul-body binding/loosing formula — among the most important substrate teachings in the corpus. The macrocosm-as-human-body mapping (¶11-12) and the soul-binding formula (¶35, reversed in ¶38) are classic correspondential substrate: both sides of every mapping stay within the cosmic system. The five watch-districts of the Living Spirit's sons (¶19-28) form a complete cosmological architecture. The chapter shows clear editorial fatigue: substrate dominates ¶11-43, institutional overlay increases in the progressive-sin sequence (¶44-50), and the apostolate section (¶59-66) is entirely institutional. The editorial_bridge material in ¶36 (idol worship) is diagnostic — the five-fold overlay teaching pivots mid-paragraph to contemporary religious polemic. The progressive sin-attack sequence (¶43-50) preserves substrate structure (the five-fold inward progression from consideration to mind) but is heavily overlaid with institutional description of church community responses.

paragraphs.core_text: the Light Mi[nd] is this one who shall come and assume the saints. [...] He too is one among the gods [...] many gods are with him. [...] [W]hen he enters withi[n the body of] the flesh and binds the ol[d ma]n with his five counsels, he [set]s his five [couns]els upon him in the five limbs [of his] body.
paragraphs.removed_material: Dialogue frame: 'Once again, at one of the times, a disciple questioned the [apostle], saying to him: You have told us that... [You sai]d it to us like this:... You have also told us:'
paragraphs.temporal_note: The disciple recaps previous substrate teaching about the five counsels in the five limbs — this IS the soul-body binding formula being referenced. Frame wraps substantive cosmological content.

paragraphs.core_text: [So], no[w], where is he? In that the old man is chained in the body! For I see how rebellions arise there despite his bondage, from time to time.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Substantive cosmological question in the Persian dialogue tradition. Defines the teaching problem: how do rebellions arise despite the binding? This structures the entire watch-district teaching that follows.

paragraphs.core_text: If then he is a great God, unchanging and im/measurable, how could he come and appear in the smallness of the bo[dy]?
paragraphs.removed_material: Frame formula: 'Also, secondly, I a[s]k you:'
paragraphs.temporal_note: Substantive cosmological question about the contraction of a great being into a small space — answered later by the taproot analogy (¶53).

paragraphs.core_text: [...] a holy one is the Mind, and he is pure; [...] the defilement of this body?
paragraphs.removed_material: Frame formula: 'The third thing I want you to recount to [me ...]'
paragraphs.temporal_note: Substantive question about purity/defilement paradox. Much damaged by lacunae. Answered by ¶54.

paragraphs.core_text: Fourthly: If truly the Light Mind exists in [the s]aints, why is his likeness not displayed to us, the way that he is?
paragraphs.temporal_note: Enumerated substantive question. 'Fourthly' is an enumeration marker integral to the teaching structure. Answered by ¶52.
Fifth question about Mani's apostolate — this is biographical/institutional content, not a cosmological question. Sets up the institutional section (¶59-66).
Pure frame formula — disciple's entreaty. High dialogue_frame score (26.67) confirms.
Mani's response referencing 'my church' — institutional language in dialogue frame. No cosmological content.
Disciple restates desire to know about the Light Mind. Formulaic exchange before teaching begins.
Rhetorical preparation: 'I will make the living fountain overflow for the thirsty.' Figurative language but functioning as pedagogical frame, not systematic teaching.

paragraphs.core_text: All the error, when the en[e]my of the lights constructed it, he constructed after the likeness of a man. The head of the universe is the beginning of the garments. [H]is neck is the nape of the garm[ents]. His stomach is the five unfolded ones (?), which a[re ... ] of the garm[e]nts. His ribs are all the firmament[s]. His navel is the sphere of the stars and the signs of the zodiac. And, also, [the par]ts [that] come from his navel to his hip are [...] that come from the sphere t[o the corne]rs of the four worlds. His loins are the th[ree eart]hs that are below [...] upon the head of the Porter. His [...] from the [...] to the earth upon which the Porter [is stood] firm. His shins and his feet a[re ...] and the entire zone that belongs [...]
paragraphs.removed_material: Dialogue frame: 'Then speaks the apostle to him:'
paragraphs.temporal_note: The body-cosmos correspondence begins. The universe is constructed as a human body: head=garments (heavens), ribs=firmaments, navel=zodiac, loins=three earths, feet=zone. Classic correspondential substrate — both sides stay within the cosmic system.

paragraphs.core_text:
⟨p.91⟩
His heart is mankind. His liver is the four-footed animals. His lung is the race of birds that [fly in] the air. His spleen is the race of fish that swim in the waters. His kidneys are the world of reptiles that creep [up]on the earth. His outer skin is the wall that [... which] surrounds the piercing and the great fire. His [...] the vessels of the great fire. His [...] of darkness. His gall is the [... His] great intestine is the breadth of the great [...] of the worlds. His veins [...] all [the spri]ngs and wells. His e[yes (?) ...] His feet are his [...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure body-cosmos correspondence continuing from ¶11. Organ→cosmic domain: heart=mankind, liver=quadrupeds, lung=birds, spleen=fish, kidneys=reptiles, skin=surrounding wall, veins=springs and wells. Every mapping stays internal to the cosmic system. This is the remnant of the body-cosmos teaching tradition.

paragraphs.core_text: This is how each of the worlds h[ave been ha]rmonised (?). Five gods are fastened in him. [...] they are his soul and his life [...] man is a sinner [...] the Living Spirit and the Ambassador [...] the five sleepless guardians.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Summary: five gods as soul/life of the cosmic body, with the Living Spirit, Ambassador, and five sleepless guardians. Fragmentary but clearly substrate — cosmological hierarchy.

paragraphs.core_text: He has [...] the Keeper of Splendour, the mind that is [...] in the wo[r]ld of the mind that is above. He has [...] who]le [...] of the powers of hea[ven that] are in [...] of the great King of Honour, [who is the thought that exists i]n the seventh firmament. He has humbled [...] also of the Adamant of Lig[h]t, who is the insight [... ] from {} he has given [...] because of lust [... He has] also appointed the King of Glory, who is the coun[sel ...] patience over the three images; that of wind, that of fire, and that of water. He has handed over to him the [...] do evilness. [...] the Porter, who is the consideration [...] the wi]sdom in the [...] which is below. He has made him [...] the foundation [below ...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Five-fold faculty mapping: Keeper of Splendour=mind (above), King of Honour=thought (seventh firmament), Adamant of Light=insight, King of Glory=counsel/patience (over three images of wind/fire/water), Porter=consideration/wisdom (below). This is the quintessential substrate: cosmic being → intellectual faculty → cosmic station. All three sides stay within the system.

paragraphs.core_text:
⟨p.92⟩
Furthermore: The Ambassador refined from them five intellectuals of life. Also, the summons and the obedience were situated there. Now, they made six sons of the Living Spirit, together with the six sons of the First Man!
paragraphs.temporal_note: Emanation hierarchy: Ambassador refines five intellectuals, summons and obedience make the sixth. High substrate score (34.21). The enumeration of six sons of the Living Spirit with six sons of the First Man is systematic cosmological structure.

paragraphs.core_text: Further: The Ambassador placed in them the great Mind; who is the Pillar of Glory, the Perfect Man.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Highest substrate score in chapter (44.44). Identification: great Mind = Pillar of Glory = Perfect Man. Triple cosmic identification.

paragraphs.core_text: Furthermore: Jesus the Youth was set there; who is the image of the living word, of the utterance and the obedience.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Bridge connective flagged but this continues the emanation sequence from ¶15-16. Jesus the Youth is a cosmic figure (not the historical Jesus), identified as the image of the living word / utterance and obedience. Completes the cosmic architecture. 'Furthermore' is a sequence marker within the enumeration.

paragraphs.core_text: He has made strong these camps, those above and those below [...], (so that) each one of them will be secure in the circuit of his watch-district, so that neither uprising nor treachery are made in his watch-district.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Establishes the watch-district system. Both sides cosmic: camps above and below → watch-districts → security against uprising. This sets up the five watch-district narratives that follow.

paragraphs.core_text: And look, see! The Keeper of Splendour is set firm in the great mind, in the camp above the prison of the bound ones, for he brings to nothing all the gloom of death. An[d a] treachery came about, and an uprising! The Sin abor[te]d, [it t]angled i]n with the soul. It became mixed with this light that it expelled toward the image of the Ambassador. It went [...] in the third firmament that is above the watch-t[ower ...] the Keeper of Splendour. From that place also it tangled in with the light. It was detached and came down to that which is dry and that which is moist. It [fashio]ned the trees [up]on the dry (land); but in the sea it immediat[ely] took form and made a great uprising in the sea.
paragraphs.temporal_note: First watch-district narrative: Keeper of Splendour (mind). Sin's treachery — aborting, tangling with light, mixing, descending to form trees on land and uprising in sea. Entirely within the cosmic system.

paragraphs.core_text: Again, look, see! The great King of Honour, who is the thought, he is in the thi[r]d firmament. He is made [...] with wrath. And an uprising came about! A treachery and a[n] anger happened in his camp. The watchers of heaven, who came down to the earth in his watch-district, they did all the deeds of treachery. They have revealed crafts in the world and have unveiled to people the mysteries of heaven. An uprising came about, and a destruction, on the earth [... ] to it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Second watch-district: King of Honour (thought) in the third/seventh firmament. The watchers narrative is the Enochic tradition integrated into the cosmic architecture — cosmic history, not contemporary application.

paragraphs.core_text: The Adamant [...] the fulfillment. He is set firm upo[n ...] and a treachery came about in his camp; the occasion when the abortions fell to the earth. They formed Adam and Eve. They begat them so as to reign through them in the world. They fashioned every object of lust upon the earth. The entire world was filled by their lust.
paragraphs.removed_material: Institutional extension: 'Also, {} they persecute the churches. They kill the apostles and the righteous in the watch-district of the Adamant of Light, time after time, and from generation to generation.' — 'churches' and 'apostles' reach into the editor's contemporary world.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Third watch-district: Adamant of Light (insight). Core narrates the abortions forming Adam and Eve — cosmic history. The final sentence extends the narrative to persecution of churches and apostles, crossing from cosmic to contemporary. The seam is at 'Also, {} they persecute...'

paragraphs.core_text: Once again: In the watch of the great King of Glory, wh[o] is the great counsel, he who exercises authority over the thre[e] wheels. A [dis]turbance came about, and an affliction, for [they were ... ] pained and oppressed in the three earths. After the Ambassador displayed his image, the paths closed to their [...] their ascent was impeded by them [...] the w[ind], the water, and the fire ascend on them.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fourth watch-district: King of Glory (counsel) over the three wheels. Disturbance in three earths, impeded ascent of wind/water/fire. Both sides cosmic: cosmic ruler → cosmic domain → cosmic process.

paragraphs.core_text: [O]nce again: In the watch of the Porter, he who humiliates [...] upr]ising of the abysses below [...] bent, the fastenings underneath were loosened [...] in the foundation below.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fifth watch-district: Porter (consideration/wisdom) at the foundation below. Uprising of abysses, fastenings loosened. Very fragmentary but clearly substrate — cosmic structure.

paragraphs.core_text: On account of the earthquake that happened in the watch of the Keeper of Splen[dour], the Pillar of Glory came forth; as it [...] helper of the Keeper of Splendour. It bore up under all [burden]s.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Response to first watch treachery: Pillar of Glory aids the Keeper of Splendour. High substrate score (22.22). Cosmic beings responding to cosmic crisis — both sides internal.

paragraphs.core_text: Conversely, because of the treachery and the uprising that happened in the watch of the great King of Honour, which is the watchers who came down to earth from the heavens; four angels were called upon about them. They bound the watche[r]s with an eternal chain, in the prison of the blackened ones (?). [Th]ey obliterated their children from upon the earth.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Response to second watch treachery: four angels bind the watchers. Enochic tradition fully integrated into the cosmic architecture. Both sides stay within the system.

paragraphs.core_text: [Th]en, again, the abortions descended in the watch of the Adamant and begat Adam and Eve; because of that great treachery wh[ich] happened, and the mystery of wickedness, he sent Jesus [...] the prayer of the five sons. He assumed them [...] the abortions. He fastened them beneath the [...] the mind of Adam.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Response to third watch treachery: cosmic Jesus sent to awaken Adam. 'Jesus' here is the cosmic figure (Jesus the Splendour), not the historical Jesus. 'The mind of Adam' — the faculty system applied to the primal human. Both sides cosmic.

paragraphs.core_text:
⟨p.94⟩
Also, because of the earthquake that happened in these three earths, and in that the paths were hindered and the springs of wind and water and fire were impeded, Jesus cast himself down. He assumed Eve; and he straightened the tracks of the [win]d, the water, and the fire. He opened the springs for them, and he set [in ord]er the path of their ascent.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Response to fourth watch treachery: cosmic Jesus opens the paths of wind, water, and fire. Cosmic process vocabulary: springs, tracks, paths, ascent. Both sides internal.

paragraphs.core_text: Once [again]: Since the earth beneath the Porter was loose[ned from] the fastenings that [...] because of this too Jesus went down, assuming [Ev]e until he reached tha[t] place. [H]e set in [or]der and stre[ng]th[ened] the fastenings beneath. He returned, [he came] up to his [...] rest.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Response to fifth watch treachery: Jesus strengthens the foundation beneath the Porter. Completes the five-fold watch-response sequence. Cosmic narrative.

paragraphs.core_text: Look at all these watches of the zon[e], the ones in which these great gods are master, w[atch]ing over them [...]. Uprisings have happened, and treachery, in them. The [...] in them from time to time; with a great hum[iliati]on, until they humbled the powers of the enmity.
paragraphs.removed_material: Dialogue frame: 'Then speaks the a[po]stl[e] to him:'
paragraphs.temporal_note: Summary of the five watch-district teaching. Transitions from the macrocosm to the microcosm. The summary recapitulates the substrate teaching.

paragraphs.core_text: So also is this body! A mighty power lives here, even if it is small in its stature. Nevertheless, Sin dwells within, and the old man who is lodged in it. Certainly he is cruel, with great cunning; until the Lig/ht Mind finds how to humble this body, and drive it [according to] his pleasure.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The pivot from macrocosm to microcosm. The body is the watch-district of the Light Mind, with Sin and the old man as the internal adversary. Both sides remain within the cosmic system — this IS the macrocosm-microcosm correspondence.

paragraphs.core_text: Just so, in the w[atch-]districts of his great outer brothers, they who are masters in the zone: in them, in the great body, the earthquake and treachery happened from time to time. So, also, is the watch-district of the Mind, which is the body of the flesh. Sin raises [up], from time to time, its agitations in the body.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Explicit macrocosm-microcosm parallel: watch-districts in the zone → watch-district of the Mind in the body. Both sides cosmic. The mapping is the teaching.

paragraphs.core_text: the powers of light are good. The beginning and the end are unveiled to them. All that they do is being done with correct judgement. Indeed, because of this they may permit the enmity to initiate error, and do its pleasure for a moment. Then they seize [...] they have acted first with a righteous judgement.
paragraphs.removed_material: Pedagogical framing: 'Now you, understand thus, that'
paragraphs.temporal_note: Teaching about the strategic nature of light powers — they permit evil temporarily because they see the whole cosmic process. Both sides stay within the system: light powers → enmity → judgement. The 'Now you, understand thus' is editorial address.

paragraphs.core_text: These gods, in that [...] are great and mighty ones. And each one of them is enclosed and hard pressed in this place wherein he is set; like trees holding to their taproot. So also this is how each one of them has held to his taproot in the world, according to the k[ind] of place in which he is set, bearing up till [...]
paragraphs.removed_material: Frame reference: 'And [with resp]ect to this other (question) that you have put forward: How may the Light Mind come, this great and honoured mighty one, and assume this little body of the flesh? Again, look, see!'
paragraphs.temporal_note: Answers the second question (how can a great God appear in a small body). The taproot analogy: each god is enclosed in its place like a tree holding to its taproot. This is substrate — it describes the NATURE of cosmic beings' self-contraction. The frame reference to the earlier question is editorial.

paragraphs.core_text: the world is set firm, being ordered [...] the five sons of the Living Spirit in all its members [...]. Sin took this body out from [the] la[nd (?) ... co]nstructed it in its members. It took its [bod]y from the five b]odies of Darkness. (Sin) constructed the body. Yet, its [sou]l i[t] took from the five shining gods.
paragraphs.removed_material: Pedagogical framing: 'Now, also, happen you know [...]'
paragraphs.temporal_note: Key transition: from macrocosm to body. The world ordered by five sons of Living Spirit → Sin constructs body from five bodies of Darkness, takes soul from five shining gods. This sets up the binding formula in ¶35. High substrate score (18.46).

paragraphs.core_text: (Sin) bou]nd (the soul) in the five members of the body. It bound the mind in bone; the thought in sinew; the insight in vein; the counsel in flesh; the consideration in ski[n].
paragraphs.temporal_note: THE QUINTESSENTIAL SUBSTRATE. The soul-body binding formula: mind=bone, thought=sinew, insight=vein, counsel=flesh, consideration=skin. Highest substrate score in the chapter (60.61). This is pure correspondential mapping — cosmic faculty → body member. Both sides stay entirely within the system. This is the ancient binding formula preserved in the Coptic.

paragraphs.core_text: (Sin) set f[ast] its five powers: its mind upon the mind of the soul; its thought upon the thought of the soul; its insight upon the insight of the soul; its counsel upon the counsel of the soul; its consider[atio]n upon the consideration of the soul. It placed its five [an]gels and authorities upon the five members of the soul, which it had brought in and bound in the flesh.
paragraphs.removed_material: Editorial bridge — application to contemporary idolatry: 'They [...], pronouncing to the soul and continually leading it on to every evil thi[n]g, to all the sins of lust, to the worship of idols, to erroneous opinions, to humili[ation]; in the humiliation of slavery! As it is set fast, wors[hipping] the things that [...] will not remain; making obeisance [...] idols of wood and gold and silver [...] worshipping beasts that are unclean and polluted! They are ugly in their appearances and their forms.' One side of the mapping reaches into contemporary religious practices (idol worship, obeisance to wood/gold/silver images).
paragraphs.temporal_note: The substrate continues the five-fold system: Sin overlays its five powers upon the soul's five faculties. Then the editorial bridge crosses into the contemporary world: 'worship of idols,' 'idols of wood and gold and silver,' 'worshipping beasts.' The seam is after 'bound in the flesh.' The editorial_bridge score (2.05) confirms.

paragraphs.core_text: (The soul) assumed error and forgetfulness. It for[go]t its essence and its race and its kindred; kn[ow]ing not the door of the place to pray to him, nor call up to him. It became hostile to its father [...] itself, being wicked [...] its own light [...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Describes the soul's fall into error and forgetfulness after the binding. 'Forgot its essence and its race and its kindred' — the soul's amnesia of cosmic origin. Both sides cosmic: bound soul → forgetfulness of divine nature.

paragraphs.core_text: The Light Mind comes and finds the soul [...] it assuming it in the [...] its wisdom [...] he shall become for it [...] the bonds [...] members in the body. He shall loosen the m[ind of the soul and relea]se it from the bone. He shall release the th[ought of the soul] from the sinew; and s[o] bind the thought [of the Sin in] the sinew. He shall release the insight of the soul from the vei[n]; and so bind the insight of the Sin in the vein. [He sh]all loosen the counsel of the soul, and release it from the flesh; and so bind the counsel of the Sin in the flesh. He shall release the consideration of the soul from the skin; and bin[d] the consideration of the Sin in the skin.
paragraphs.temporal_note: THE REVERSAL FORMULA. The Light Mind systematically reverses the binding of ¶35: mind released from bone / Sin's mind bound in bone; thought released from sinew / Sin's thought bound in sinew; and so on through all five. This is pure substrate — the correspondential reversal. Each faculty is released and its dark counterpart bound in the same member. The structural perfection of this five-fold reversal is the hallmark of the oldest teaching layer.

paragraphs.core_text:
⟨p.97⟩
This is how he shall release the members of the soul, and make them free from the five members of Sin. Conversely, these five members of Sin, which were loose, he shall bind them.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Summary of the binding/loosing formula: soul's five members freed, Sin's five members bound. The reversal principle stated explicitly.

paragraphs.core_text: He shall set right the members of the soul; form and purify them, and construct a new man of them, a child of righteousness. [And] when [he] fashions and const[r]ucts and purifies the new man; then he shall bring forth five great living members out from the five great memb[ers]. And he places them in the members of the new man. He shall place his m[ind], which is love, in the mind of the new man. Also, the th[oug]ht, which is faith, he shall pl[ace in] the thought of the new man; whom he shall purify. His insight, which [is perfection, he shall place] in the insight of the new man. His counsel, which [is] patience, he shall place in his counsel. Also, [w]isdom, which is his consideration, in the consideration of the new m[an]. He shall make the image of the word pure from the word of Sin; and he adds to it his word, so that his [...] becomes nourisher and strengthener [...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Five-fold virtue mapping: mind=love, thought=faith, insight=perfection, counsel=patience, consideration=wisdom. These five virtues replace the five bound faculties in the 'new man.' Both sides stay within the cosmic system — faculty → virtue. The 'new man' is a cosmic process term (the transformed person), not an institutional one.

paragraphs.core_text: Now, when he shall perf[ect ... the tw]elve members. This [is how ...] and his wisdom. His [...] becomes righteous, as he perf[ects ...] While formerly he was running [...] but instead of this, now he runs [...] his road and his path and his [...] also [he mounts up] to the heights, to the great aeons [...] thus the old man is bound in the [...] and his lust, his [...] his foolishness in these five members of the bo[dy ...] the dark spirit is imprisoned with them in a bond and in severe misery.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Completion of transformation: twelve members perfected, old man bound, dark spirit imprisoned in the five members. Very fragmentary but the substrate structure is clear — it narrates the cosmic process to completion.

paragraphs.core_text: Also, the new man reigns by his love, by hi[s] faith, by his perfection, by his patience, and by his wisdom. Yet, his king [...] the Light Mind, he w[ho is] king over the totality. He re[igns] o[ver it according to] his pleasure. While the members [...], thus Sin is imprisoned. Still, the Light Mind is king, and an affliction may arise in the body from t[im]e to time.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The new man reigns through the five virtues (love, faith, perfection, patience, wisdom — the same sequence as ¶40). The Light Mind as king. Sin imprisoned but able to generate affliction — this sets up the progressive-attack sequence. Both sides cosmic.

paragraphs.core_text: There are occasions when Sin shall mount up with its foolishness; and it disturbs the consideration, and it clouds the wisdom and the understanding of the person. It causes truth to be split into doubt in him, and he utters some foo[li]sh words and some [...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: First stage of Sin's progressive attack: Sin disturbs the CONSIDERATION (outermost faculty = skin). Clouds wisdom. This follows the five-fold system from outer to inner. Substrate — the attack is described within the body-cosmos framework.

Seam flag correctly identifies institutional extension. 'The church,' 'the teachers,' 'the presbyters' — specific institutional vocabulary. Describes the community's response to a member's foolishness. The faculty vocabulary (consideration, wisdom) is used within an institutional framework. Classified as institutional rather than mixed because the paragraph's PURPOSE is to describe the church's role.

paragraphs.core_text: Sin mount up again, another time, from the consideration to the counsel. It takes his patience f[rom him], and bestows upon him faint-heartedness and hurt. [...] A battle and a war shall arise (between) the Light Mind and the Sin in the counsel [...]
paragraphs.removed_material: Institutional context: 'Now, if he shall not accept the rebuke and the edification of his brethren and his helpers; then shall...' and 'And the [si]n is displ[ayed] in the midst of his brethren. His [...] for every [thing] that he shall do [...] advice of his brethren, and he becomes [...] the [fo]olishness...' and 'they sh]all group together and become [...] there, and they cause him to cease from the [...] and they put him straight in his place another ti[me ...] his compa[nio]ns in his struggle.'
paragraphs.temporal_note: Second stage: Sin rises from consideration to COUNSEL (flesh). Takes patience — patience is the virtue of counsel (¶40). The substrate progressive attack continues through the faculty system. Institutional overlay describes community correction.

paragraphs.core_text: Sin shall rise [...] and clothe him with lust and vanity and pride.
paragraphs.removed_material: Institutional behavioral description: 'He separates from his teacher and his brethren. [He sh]all always [w]ant to go in and to come out alone. He shall want to eat and to drink alone, a solitary man. [He sh]all always want to walk alone. Indeed, this is the [si]gn that the familiarity of his brethren does not act on him.' Also conditional frame: 'If again the [...] to that place, then again...'
paragraphs.temporal_note: Brief substrate fragment: Sin rises and clothes with lust/vanity/pride. The rest is institutional description of behavioral signs within the community. The substrate portion is minimal but preserves the progressive-attack structure.

paragraphs.core_text: Sin shall mount up, the thought of death, to his thought. He shall [...] a vanity; and causes his f[ai]th and his truth to le[a]ve him.
paragraphs.removed_material: Conditional frame: 'Should he again not [...] his heart from lust; again...' and institutional response: 'When the sign of his foolishness will be [dis]played, and his reputation spreads in the church, the [wis]e ones of the church shall gather to him; so [that] they may set right his [heart], and encourage it with God's edification. If now he took [the adv]ice of his brethren, and listened to [...] and set himself apart from his wrath and [...]'
paragraphs.temporal_note: Third stage: Sin rises to THOUGHT. 'The thought of death' replaces thought; faith and truth depart — faith is the virtue of thought (¶40). The progressive attack continues inward. Institutional overlay describes church elders' response.
Brief exhortatory/pastoral statement. Exhortation score (17.65) is the only score firing. 'It is possible he could live and be victorious over the sin' — hopeful application, not systematic teaching.

paragraphs.core_text: (Sin) shall rise up and assume his mind; and disturb his mind, which formerly was calm. It shall disrupt his love
paragraphs.removed_material: Conditional frame: 'Yet, if he shall not make this watch secure,...' and institutional manifestation: 'away from his teacher and his instructor. It shall take from his heart love of the church, and fill it full of hatred. And all his brethren become hateful before him. His brethren and his loved ones and his friends who love him; they shall be like enemies before him.'
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fourth and final stage: Sin rises to MIND (innermost faculty = bone). Disrupts love — love is the virtue of mind (¶40). The progressive attack reaches the deepest level. Institutional overlay describes the social consequences within the community.

paragraphs.core_text: The Mind, who was in him, sh[a]ll disperse from him [...] He shall be filled by evil spirits; and they deal with [him], dragging [hi]m hither and thither. [...] [He] will change and become as if a b[i]rd, were its feathers plucked out. He becomes an earthly man.
paragraphs.removed_material: Institutional context: 'Now, that person is disturbed like this, and he lets his love and his will turn from him. That person shall [himse]lf become a vessel of loss, and he separates fr[om] the church, and his end comes down to the world.' and 'and go to the apos[t]le who sent him.' and 'And he himself becomes like wordl[y] me[n].'
paragraphs.temporal_note: The cosmic process conclusion: Mind departs, evil spirits fill the void. The bird-without-feathers correspondence is striking — a vivid image for the soul stripped of its light faculties. 'He becomes an earthly man' is the cosmic reversal of the transformation. The institutional overlay references the church and the apostle.
Summary frame: 'Then, have I taught you...' Mani restates the macrocosm-microcosm correspondence but as meta-teaching reference, not new teaching. Formulaic.

paragraphs.core_text: So al[so] these watch-keepers, for they are set [...] fi[rm in] the zone, (but) they are not visible. Again, this too is the way of the Light Mind, [for he is] not visible in the body.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Answers the fourth question (¶5): why is the Light Mind not visible? Mapping: watch-keepers not visible in the zone → Light Mind not visible in the body. Both sides cosmic.

paragraphs.core_text: Also, [corr]esponding to th[ese] outer [watch-keepers]: in that while they are great, [y]et have they contorted themselves. They have [...], they have become small, to the measure of the task that is apportioned to each o[n]e [of t]hem. Again, this too is like the Mind, himse[lf] a great one, and exalted; but he is bent over and [has] become small, to this little worthless [bo]dy.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Answers the second question (¶3): how can a great God appear in a small body? Mapping: great gods contort and become small for their tasks → Mind becomes small for the body. The word 'corresponding' (ⲉⲕⲁⲧⲁ) explicitly marks the correspondential method.

paragraphs.core_text: [Even so] the gods in the outer [z]one: they are transcendent and purified, they are set [f]a[st in] the mingling of the totality, (but) are not defiled. [This too is like the] Light [Mind]. While he is placed in hi[s ...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Answers the third question (¶4): how can a pure Mind dwell in a defiled body? Mapping: gods in the zone not defiled by mixture → Mind not defiled in the body. Fragmentary but the correspondence is clear.

paragraphs.core_text:
⟨p.100⟩
Again, behold the mightiness and the activity of the Light Mind: how vast he is over all the watch-districts of the body! He stays fast at his camp. He shuts off all deliberations of the body from the beguilements of Sin. He limits them and distributes them out. He sets them down at his pleasure.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Describes the Light Mind's governance of the body's watch-districts. Process vocabulary: shuts off, limits, distributes. The body is the cosmic domain; the Light Mind is the cosmic governor. Both sides stay within the system.

paragraphs.core_text: Also, he does another work, surpassing and ex/ceeding (these). He bestows a great spirit upon the ele/ct one. Indeed, now may you find him, as he stands on the earth, [r]ising up in his heart and ascending to the Father, the G[o]d of truth. He who exists and is established above all the things of loss. [Onc]e again, he may push dow[n] in his insight and his consideration, and descend to the land of Darkness, from where the Darkness has poured forth. His heart shall run and touch everything, as it [...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: The Light Mind's supreme work: enabling cosmic traversal through the faculties. Ascending through the heart to the Father; descending through insight and consideration to the land of Darkness. Both sides stay within the cosmic system. 'Elect one' is Manichaean institutional vocabulary but may be a Coptic translation choice for the substrate concept of 'the transformed one.' The cosmological content is overwhelmingly dominant. Flagged for uncertainty on 'elect one.'

Frame: 'Then he says to that disciple: I have taught you the deeds of the Light Mind!' The perception teaching ('whoever has an open eye') is generic wisdom, not systematic correspondence. Transitional frame to the apostolate section.
Transition to the apostolate section. 'My work... my leadership.' Mani's self-reference. Pure frame.

Mani's apostolate claims: 'I, a single Manichaios, I have come to the world alone.' References races, kindreds, gold, silver, brass — worldly powers submitting to him. Apostolic narrative, not cosmic teaching.

Mani's comparison of his mission to worldly conquest. 'I have conquered without breastplate and without armour distant cities by the word of God.' Apostolic narrative — reaching outside the cosmic system into historical claims.
Kings, nobles, officials striving against Mani. Historical-biographical narrative about Mani's persecution and triumph. Institutional/apostolic layer.
Mani's third claim: giving freedom to his spiritual children. Institutional — describes his community work.

Mani's fourth claim: the 'breastplate of wisdom' for his children. Contains some exhortatory overtone ('so it is also like this for my children') but the primary function is apostolic boasting. Exhortation score (9.23) captures the devotional edge.

Mani's fifth claim: establishing the church. 'I have chosen... this great election,' 'I have made my church strong,' 'Apostles and ambassadors I have sent to all countries.' Highest institutional score in the chapter (11.24). Pure church-building narrative.
Apostolic succession claim: Mani surpasses all former apostles except Jesus. 'This hard generation' anchors to the editor's/Mani's present. Institutional.

Cosmic vocabulary ('gods and the angels and mankind, and all the spirits and the living souls') but used within Mani's self-referential claim: 'opened by me.' The cosmic language serves institutional purpose — Mani's mission extends to all cosmic beings. Still institutional despite substrate vocabulary.

Closing devotional frame: disciples promise to 'make ourselves strong in your faith; and persevere in your commandments.' Formulaic closure typical of Kephalaia chapters. Exhortation and dialogue frame interwoven.
